ctx.x: With the, uh, with the guy. I mean, you just didn't play your art or anything. You, you, if you were a musician, well, that's what you were, and you weren't anything else.

Uh, incidentally, uh, Joe, Joe was a great, uh, Shakespearean fan, you know? Joe read Shakespeare every night of his life, man. And, I think when he graduated from high school, his mother had given him a, uh, oh, I think comedy tragedy and something or else, you know, all about Shakespeare. And, uh, it got to be like a tonic with him. Uh, you might say a, a sleep inducer. He had to read a few lines of Shakespeare every night before he went to sleep, you know? And, I mean, it was things like that that made a…

Well, Johnny Lane is the same. He sits up on the stand. This is a guy from Chicago that studied under Jimmy Newman. He sits up on the stand. On the stand. He might have had it right the first time. But anyways, he sits on the stand and reads Shakespeare, you know, between numbers. And Joe's Boonies will be playing with him. And he'll say, well, the next number is dedicated to our boss. High psychiatry. You know?
